name: Tre Oiler
strengths: Oiler high-points contested fades and uses 6-6 length to box out DBs at the catch point.
Oiler eats grass with long strides on seam and vertical stems — covers ground deceptively fast for size.
Oiler adjusts to back-shoulder throws and plucks low balls without breaking stride on crossing routes.
Oiler shows functional inline length — better hand placement as a sophomore and can drive LBs on combo blocks.
weaknesses: Oiler's YAC is power strides more than elusiveness — still refining sudden breaks and layered route polish.
comparison: Oiler comps to Jake Ferguson — 6-5 / ~250 mold, balanced TE who wins with size, hands, and functional blocking before the elite household names (size-matched within ~1" of Oiler's 6-6 / 230 frame).
projection: Oiler projects as develop into the TE room, earn early F/H and special-teams snaps, then compete for a starting mismatch role — starter upside as a seam/red-zone TE.
schemeFit: Oiler fits as an F/Y hybrid who stresses the seam and red zone while the inline blocking fills out.
insiderNotes: Oiler high-points contested fades, eats grass on seam stems, and adjusts to back-shoulder balls without breaking stride. Sophomore tape shows better route stems and enough length to drive LBs on combo blocks — power YAC more than wiggle.
staffNotes: Vault film desk verified 2026-08-19 from Arrowhead freshman + 2025 sophomore Hudl. Comp size-matched within ~1–2" — not a Florida-alum default.
recruitingStory: Tre Oiler is a 4-star TE · listed 6-6 / 230 · Arrowhead (Hartland, WI) · On3 Natl #270 · Pos #12 · State #1 (WI) · Florida offered (Evan McKissack) · UF RPM ~6%.
angle: Lead with Florida's return UV this weekend on Wisconsin's top TE; McKissack offer + 2 UOVs already on file.
